Final change for PR #638, owner decision: remove the prompt signal handling. Worktree /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/wp-add-inquire (HEAD 6ecabca29 = pushed). Trail #487. (1) Delete the signal thread, the static STATE Mutex, Mode::RestoreTerminal and react() in crates/callisto-cli/src/tty.rs and the tty::prompt wrapper's signal registration; inquire already reads Ctrl-C and Esc as keys, restores the terminal and returns a cancel, which maps to CliError::Cancelled and exit 130 as now. (2) Keep only the editor rule: SIGINT ignored while $EDITOR runs via the signal_hook::flag registration (no thread, no printing), as EditorOwnsCtrlC does. (3) Remove the pty test that asserts terminal restoration after an external kill -INT at a prompt; keep one asserting that an external SIGINT at a prompt ends the process (signal 2) and writes nothing. (4) docs/specs/cli.json and the changeset: state the limit in one line: an external SIGINT at a prompt ends Callisto with default signal behaviour; run reset if the terminal is left raw. If signal-hook is now only used by the editor flag keep it; drop any dependency that became unused. The result should be smaller than now. Full gate by exit code before reporting: just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test (pty and network tests unsandboxed). Commit locally (signed), report the sha, the diff stat and each gate's exit code. Do not push and do not touch findings; the lead does both. Scope is fixed: change nothing outside this list. Rules (from the lead session close-gap-for-alpha). Be thorough before a push: a push costs a paid review, so find problems locally first.
- Read AGENTS.md. Prefer a type or private constructor over a check; delete checks a type makes redundant; fix sibling call sites in the same PR.
- A check, preview, dry run or test must run on exactly the structure the real path executes (one shared graph or derivation, the real tool), never a projection, copy or re-implementation. When fixing a failing or flaky test, assert the measured behaviour still happens.
- No new traits, async or frameworks. No new error codes, JSON keys or flags without asking the lead.
- Work in a named worktree off fresh origin/main. Write the failing test first for behaviour changes.
- Before reporting a change as ready to push, run the AGENTS.md gate in full and judge each by exit code: `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test` (workspace-wide, not just the touched crate; tests elsewhere read scripts, specs and error registries). Run network/pty tests unsandboxed. Iterate with scoped `cargo test -p` while working.
- If you change a public signature in callisto-manifests or callisto-model, also run `just fuzz-check` (the fuzz crate is outside the workspace, so crate tests miss it).
- Run `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff` only for new decision logic, not for merges, renames, docs, CI or tests; never commit mutants.out*.
- Merges and conflict resolutions: resolve, run the touched crate's tests, push. Nothing else.
- Changeset (`cargo run -p callisto-cli -- add ...`) only for user-visible changes, written for users.
- Every push triggers a paid review. Before reporting, run the checklist in /Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/d58474bb/tmp/review-checklist.md against your full diff. Push once, only after the lead has read your diff and says push; for an existing PR, commit locally and report the worktree and sha first.
- Signed commits, no session trailer. Merge the latest origin/main right before pushing (no rebase, no force-push). Push with git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>, confirm with git ls-remote, link the given trail, open with entire trail ci-pr.
- Trails are semantic outcomes shared by many PRs. Never change a trail's title or description (no `entire trail update` on it, no `entire trail create` to rename it). Put PR-specific text in the PR body with `gh pr edit <n> --body-file`. Link your branch to the trail the lead named; if your work does not fit that trail's outcome, ask the lead instead of linking it anyway.
- If CI fails, fix that failure only. If Entire raises findings, fix only wrong results, broken recovery, security issues or checks that cannot fail; report the rest to the lead.
- Report to the lead (close-gap-for-alpha) in under 5 lines: PR, sha, what you ran.
- CARGO_BUILD_JOBS is cores/5; never run two cargo builds in one worktree.

**`callisto add` starts from what you changed**: packages changed since their last release are listed first, marked and already ticked, so a typical changeset is Enter, pick bumps, type a summary.

- Each answer stays on screen, the prompts show their keys, and long package lists page.
- Before writing, a review lists each package's bump and the summary; afterwards `add` prints the next step.
- Leave the summary empty to write a longer one, with bullets, in `$VISUAL` or `$EDITOR`. If that editor cannot start, `add` warns and asks for the summary inline, keeping your other answers.
- Esc or Ctrl-C at any `add` or `init` question cancels: it prints `Cancelled, nothing written.`, restores the terminal and exits 130.
- If Callisto cannot tell which packages changed, it warns once and lists every package unticked instead of failing.
- With `--format json`, `add` and `init` never prompt: they ask for `--package` or `--yes` instead.

# Interactive CLI contract (add, init) - decided 2026-11-23, owner-approved direction

When prompts run
- stdin AND stderr are terminals and output is text: prompts.
- --format json, or stdin or stderr not a terminal: never prompt. add without flags -> E214; init without --yes -> E240; each names the flags to pass.
- Blank or whitespace --summary: error before any prompt.

Ending a run
- Completed: path written; next-step line on stderr; exit 0.
- Esc or Ctrl-C at any prompt: "Cancelled, nothing written."; exit 130.
- Declining the review / write confirmation: "Cancelled, nothing written."; exit 0.
- Editor saves nothing or exits non-zero: "Cancelled, nothing written."; exit 0.
- External kill -INT at a prompt: default signal behaviour (signal 2), nothing written; documented limit: terminal may need `reset`.
- SIGINT while $EDITOR runs (unix): ignored by Callisto (git launch_editor precedent); the editor decides. No signal thread anywhere.

Editor and inputs
- $VISUAL else $EDITOR; blank = unset; none -> inline summary prompt.
- Unusable editor (split error, not found, non-UTF-8): one warning naming the variable and command, then the inline prompt, answers kept.
- Whitespace-only inline summary: re-prompt.
- Changed packages first and ticked, exactly as status reports; detection failure -> one warning, all unticked.
- JSON mode: exactly one report on stdout; notes once on stderr.

init and origin
- Missing or non-hosted origin: one note; preview and init continue unbound; the remote value is never printed.
- --workflow / --artifact-target without a hosted origin: E299, help names git remote get-url --push origin / set-url --push.

Exit codes: 0 success or decline; 1 error; 2 usage; 130 cancelled at a prompt.

The full gate is running in the background (pre-push, lint, doc-check, test). I'll report once it finishes. Nothing has been committed or pushed yet.

So far:
- **Signal handling removed.** The signal thread, the static `STATE` mutex, `Mode::RestoreTerminal`, `react()` and the prompt wrapper's signal registration are gone from `tty.rs`.
- **Editor rule kept.** SIGINT is ignored while `$EDITOR` runs, using a `signal_hook::flag` registration. The default action comes back when the editor exits.
- **Dependencies.** `crossterm` is dropped as a direct dependency. `signal-hook` stays, without its `iterator` feature.
- **Tests.** The terminal-restoration test is replaced by one asserting that an external SIGINT at a prompt ends the process with signal 2 and writes nothing.
- **Docs.** `cli.json` and the changeset state the `reset` limit in one line.
- **E343 on cancel.** `main.rs` now renders `CliError::Cancelled` through the normal error renderer, so E343 and its help show. The message, stderr and exit 130 are unchanged. The four exit-130 pty tests now assert E343.
- **New pty tests for the contract rows.** I added tests for these cases:
  - Declining the add review.
  - An unusable editor, both a split error and non-UTF-8 output.
  - Declining the init write.
  - Init with `--format json` on a terminal.
- **Detection-failure warning.** The only test is the unit test. I couldn't trigger the failure through the real binary, because without git the workspace is rejected earlier (E058).

The first `just pre-push` failed only on formatting, which `cargo fmt` fixed.
